newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian police detain Moslems in mosque raid.
newsitem.headline: Russian police detain Moslems in mosque raid.

text.p: A squad of special interior ministry police raided a mosque in central Moscow and briefly detained around 20 worshippers, police said on Wednesday.
They gave no explanation for the raid, which took place late on Tuesday, but Moslem leaders reacted with indignation.

"The police behaved extremely rudely towards the worshippers, entering a place of prayer with weapons and without removing their shoes," Ekho Moskvy radio quoted Abdul-Vakhed Niyazov, head of the Union of Moslems of Russia, as saying.
The Moslems, who included ethnic Chechens and Ingushis from southern Russia, were beaten before being released, he said.
The radio reported that Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov and other officials would visit the mosque later on Wednesday "to clarify the circumstances of yesterday's incident".
Russia has had a policy of religious tolerance since the collapse of the atheistic Soviet Union in 1991 but remains nervous about the influence of Islam, especially in its southern regions.
Its army waged a bloody 21-month campaign against separatists in predominantly-Moslem Chechnya, where a delicate ceasefire now prevails.
